_comment: Manifests that label canvases with an image counter rather than a folio.
For a straightforwardly scanned book the two are related by
where the offset counts the covers and flyleaves shot before f.1r.
Nothing in these manifests states it, so each offset here was read off the
foliation pencilled on the leaf itself, and confirmed at a second leaf far
enough away that any unnumbered insert in between would have shifted it.
Add an entry only with two confirmed checks: a wrong offset mislinks every
folio in the manuscript silently, which is far worse than no link at all.

BBR 9391.note: KBR labels these Seq. N. Pencil foliation upper right.

W. 88.note: Stanford/Digital Walters labels these Page N. Pencil foliation upper right of the leaf, left of the colour chart.

W. 87.note: Stanford/Digital Walters labels these Page N.

Lambeth 233.note: Lambeth Palace labels these by image number. Pencil foliation upper right.

Jacquemart 1.note: Institut de France labels these by image number. The scan is low resolution; read the corner at native size (region/full, no upscaling) rather than from a downscaled page.

St. Omer 5.note: Odd offset, so even canvases are versos and carry no foliation. Probing canvas 300 found a blank corner; the number is on 301.

_rejected.BBR 10607: Offset is 2 at f.99 (canvas 200) but 4 at f.239 (canvas 482): an unnumbered leaf between them breaks the linear relation, so no single offset is right.
_rejected.Princeton 44-18: 795 canvases for 205 folios, nearly four per leaf. The scan holds detail shots as well as openings, so folios do not map to a fixed stride.
